tasks.short: Test recovery plans regularly and resolve failures.

steps.what: Select recovery scenarios and expected service outcomes
Prepare and approve the isolated restore execution manifest
Execute the restore plan in the isolated recovery environment
Compare restored content, configuration and service checks with expected results
Investigate failed checks and identify the recovery defect
Prepare the corrective configuration and revised recovery instructions
Check the final correction, rollback and retest manifest
outputs: accepted recovery correction and retest version

steps.what: Apply the accepted correction to the recovery configuration
inputs: accepted recovery correction and retest version

steps.what: Rerun the accepted recovery scenario and verification suite
inputs: accepted recovery correction and retest version

tasks.design: Test the backup platform's native isolated restore jobs in {OTHER}, with fixed integrity and service assertions run through {DATA_PLATFORM}. People choose scenarios, diagnose failures and review the final corrective change; initial restore, correction application and retest each use an action-specific approval bound to the actual execution manifest.
tasks.previous_blocker: Restore tests often require repeated manual commands and comparison of several evidence sources.
tasks.enabler_now: Native restore jobs and deterministic assertion suites can repeat an approved test safely.
tasks.still_hard: A passing sample does not prove every dependency or real disaster condition is covered.
tasks.human_edge: Choose meaningful failure scenarios and diagnose why recovery evidence is incomplete.

ambition.what: Run a verified isolated restore for each material change to the web service's recovery configuration.

tasks.altitude: Less command execution; more time selecting recovery scenarios and resolving uncovered dependencies.

reach.learn: Backup consistency, service dependencies and recovery objectives

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: restore orchestration and specified integrity checks can run deterministically; backup runtime is not human labour.

assumptions: Boundary is a recurring recovery exercise including corrective work. Shares are provisional hands-on labour across exercises with failures; backup transfer time and unattended restore runtime are excluded.

s1 specifies service_id, recovery_point, recovery_time_limit, expected_paths, expected_checksums, sample_record_counts and service_assertions from the service owner and prior validated recovery plan. Missing expected values are resolved manually in s1, never inferred from the restored copy.

s2 selects backup_id, isolated_target, network_policy, secret_reference and manifest_version. Native restore configuration precedes custom code. Savings apply only to current manual launch/comparison/retest work.

s7 checks exact correction content, rollback, target and retest commands after s6. Every execution approval is invalid on manifest or target change. Production failover and traffic switching are excluded and require separate approval.

Retest assertions stop on failure and leave evidence for renewed investigation; no unmodelled machine notification, production write or automatic acceptance is added. Failed cases consume retained diagnosis time or the incremental allowance.
research_questions: Do tests detect stale content, missing secrets and unreachable dependencies rather than only successful file extraction?

already_counted.description: Check recovery execution scope and targets in s2
Review correction and retest meaning in s7

incremental.description: Maintain assertions, isolated targets and failure-case regressions

approvals.approved_version: s2 final backup/isolated-target restore manifest version
s7 accepted corrective configuration version, target and rollback snapshot
s7 accepted retest execution manifest bound to corrected configuration

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 15 restore execution + 15 comparisons + 5 correction execution + 5 retest hours minus 3 upkeep = 37. Low covers half of restore execution and comparisons only, retaining manual correction and retest: 7.5+7.5-3 = 12.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend website improvements and budget the proposed work.

steps.what: Review website performance, defects and user needs
Choose improvements and define their acceptance criteria
Estimate work, integration needs and external costs for each option
Calculate cost scenarios and funding totals
Write and check the final recommendation and budget rationale
Submit the accepted proposal to the internal funding review

tasks.design: Use a controlled cost template in {SPREADSHEET}, populated from the administrator's explicit option estimates and approved rates. People still decide priorities and write the recommendation; after checking the complete proposal, a separate action submits its exact version to the funding workflow in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs depend on explicit work scope and estimates that are often missing or inconsistent.
tasks.enabler_now: Native project cost fields and validated spreadsheet formulas can reuse known estimates.
tasks.still_hard: Estimating integration risk and choosing worthwhile improvements remain judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Reject a low-cost proposal that does not address the actual user problem.

ambition.what: Give the budget owner comparable minimum, expected and expanded website-improvement cost scenarios.

tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic; improvement priorities and funding rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare a costed website improvement option set
reach.learn: Effort estimates, recurring costs and contingency assumptions

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: cost scenario arithmetic is deterministic when quantities, rates and exclusions are explicit.

assumptions: Boundary covers recommendation, budget preparation and internal submission, not funding approval or implementation. Shares are provisional current manual-work estimates.

s3 captures option_id, work_package, person_days, daily_rate, one_time_cost, recurring_period_cost, contingency_basis and estimate_source. The administrator obtains missing estimates manually within s3; delivery colleagues and suppliers retain their existing quotation work, with no transfer assumed.
Finance maintains approved cost rates and currency; team leads supply dated delivery estimates. A cost total is never generated from an improvement title alone.

Native project budgets and templates are tested before code. Existing automatic arithmetic earns no labour saving. s5 checks formula results, inclusion/exclusion scope and final recommendation meaning before s6.
a1 covers only submission of a final proposal, not spending authority. Any content, budget or reviewer queue change invalidates approval.
research_questions: Can the template make recurring costs and integration contingency visible without false precision?

already_counted.description: Verify budget totals and scope within s5

incremental.description: Maintain cost formula checks and rate references

approvals.approved_version: s5 complete improvement proposal and budget version with internal review queue

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 15 arithmetic + 5 submission hours minus 1 upkeep = 19. Low uses half the arithmetic benefit and retains manual submission: 7.5 minus 1 = 6.5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review and update webpage content and links promptly.

steps.what: Confirm requested content changes and authoritative replacement sources
Check page links, expiry dates and changed source fields
Stage the approved text and link changes in the website CMS
Approve the final page preview, meaning and destination links
Publish the accepted page revision
Check the live page and verify the intended content change

tasks.design: Configure native expiry checks, page previews and version-bound publication in {CMS}; use a link checker in {OTHER} only where the native system lacks one. Stage approved replacement fields with native bulk-edit tools, while people still resolve meaning, destination suitability and the live result before accepting the change as complete.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual link checks and repeated field edits consume time across similar pages.
tasks.enabler_now: Native CMS validation, revision previews and field-based updates can handle repeatable maintenance.
tasks.still_hard: A responding link can still lead to the wrong service or misleading information.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether changed wording and destinations still serve the page's purpose.

ambition.what: Review approaching content-expiry dates before each weekly publishing cycle.

tasks.altitude: Less link checking and repeated field editing; content accountability remains human.

reach.task: Maintain expiry dates and authoritative source references
reach.learn: CMS revisions, redirects and content ownership

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: link status checks and explicit field replacements are deterministic; destination meaning requires human review.

assumptions: Boundary includes page maintenance, publication and verification. New editorial strategy and original copywriting are separate tasks. Shares are provisional and must exclude checks already running unattended.

Content owner supplies page_id, old_field_value, replacement_value, source_reference, requested_date and expiry_date. s1 verifies them; missing source text or meaning is resolved manually, not generated.

s2 tests URLs, expiry dates and explicit field equality only. It does not mark content accurate because a URL returns successfully. s3 retains 60% for non-bulk changes and exceptions; bulk edits touch only explicitly mapped fields.

s4 checks complete final content, accessibility and actual destination meaning after staging. a1 binds page revision and publication target; further edits revoke it. No update to the live page occurs in s3.
Test native CMS features before code. This case assumes manual checking, repeat field edits and publication navigation today; current automated work earns no saving.
research_questions: Can the CMS prevent publication of a changed revision under an earlier approval?

already_counted.description: Validate staged field changes and destination meaning within s4

incremental.description: Maintain field mappings and exclude checker false positives

approvals.approved_version: s4 accepted complete page revision and website publication target

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 20 checks + 10 staging + 10 publication hours minus 2 upkeep = 38. Low gets only the 10-hour staging benefit while checks and publication remain manual: 10 minus 2 = 8. Meaning and live verification retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Install and configure a secure, logical web-server directory structure.

steps.what: Define directory layout, naming and access requirements
Prepare the final server configuration and rollback package
Review the final configuration, target and rollback
Install software and apply the accepted directory and permission configuration
Run naming, path ownership and access tests
Assess validation findings and accept or reject the installation
Write and check the installed configuration record
Commit the accepted configuration record to the service inventory

tasks.design: Test the existing configuration-management platform in {OTHER} for reusable web-server modules before writing scripts. Apply only the administrator-reviewed package to its approved target, then run explicit path, permission and naming tests; retain acceptance judgement and final record writing before a separate inventory commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated shell configuration can drift from the intended layout and permissions.
tasks.enabler_now: Declarative modules and deterministic checks can apply the reviewed configuration consistently.
tasks.still_hard: Designing secure privileges and handling legacy application assumptions remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an access design that passes syntax checks but exposes sensitive files.

ambition.what: Keep a tested directory and permission baseline for each managed web-server configuration.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated installation execution, with all security-design and release authority retained.

reach.learn: Idempotence, least privilege and rollback verification

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: reviewed declarative configuration and explicit permission tests can run without a model.

assumptions: Boundary is a software-installation case of the task on an existing server, including directory configuration and records. A physical hardware installation variant must retain its physical work; no hardware labour is silently automated. Shares are provisional.

s1 specifies target_id, software_version, document_root, directory_paths, owner, group, permission_mode, prohibited_names and application_access_requirements. s2 maps these to approved modules and a rollback version; missing requirements remain manual design work.
s3 checks actual operations, privilege changes, target and rollback after s2, not just file syntax. a1 binds the immutable package; any command or target change voids approval.

s5 assertions are derived from s1 and test permitted and prohibited access, path traversal exposure and file names. s6 retains full acceptance judgement; failure stops release and uses retained remediation/exception allowance.

s7 records target, installed_version, change_id, validation_reference and acceptance_state and checks the completed payload before s8. Native modules precede code. Existing automated deployment/runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Current manual installation and verification effort
research_questions: Do tests detect insecure readable paths and unintended permission inheritance on a realistic application?

already_counted.description: Review operational and rollback meaning in s3

incremental.description: Maintain modules, security assertions and failed-run regression cases

approvals.approved_version: s3 accepted immutable server change package, target and rollback version
s7 accepted final configuration record and service inventory destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 20 installation execution + 10 checks + 3 inventory commit hours minus 2 upkeep = 31. Low covers half the installation/check work and retains manual record commit: 10+5-2 = 13. Design, package preparation and acceptance retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeatable website operations while keeping recovery scenario design, security judgement and content approval human.
reach: Support systems administrators with tested web-service configuration and recovery modules.
role.ambitious_version: A web administrator who can demonstrate a recoverable, maintainable site with controlled changes and defensible improvement budgets.
